newsitem.title: FINLAND: METRA'S WARTSILA HAS KVAERNER ENGINE DEAL.
newsitem.headline: METRA'S WARTSILA HAS KVAERNER ENGINE DEAL.

text.p: Finnish Metra's diesel engine division Wartsila Diesel said on Thursday it would supply the main engines to Royal Caribbean Cruise Line's cruiser to be built by Norway's Kvaerner Masa-Yards .
"The order consists of six Wartsila 46 engines with total output of 75,600 kilowatts," Wartsila said in a statement, but gave no value for the deal.
The cruise ship would be the biggest in the world, it said.
"The engines will be delivered in spring 1998," it said.

The ship to be built would be the first in the Eagle series, and Wartsila said it had an option to deliver engines for another cruise liner of the same type which Masa-Yards recently won an oder to build.
A Wartsila official said the option was likely to be used since RCCL had made the order for a second cruiser official and put in an option to build a third ship.
"It is probable," said Wartsila sales director John Berg.
He said Wartsila had won the order in tight competition with German rival MAN , and that the order meant renewed confidence in Wartsila from RCCL.
